questions.question: Why should a release policy keep hard floors for critical dimensions even when it also computes a weighted diversity score?
options: Hard floors make every dimension carry the same weight.
Hard floors prevent a strong average from hiding a weak critical slice.
Hard floors eliminate the need for reviewable examples.
Hard floors guarantee that the downstream model will be fair.
questions.explanation: A weighted average can compensate for a weak dimension with stronger unrelated dimensions. A hard floor preserves the minimum evidence required for each critical slice.

questions.question: A dataset contains 10,000 prompt-response pairs averaging 2 KB each. Approximately how much raw text does one snapshot contain before storage overhead?
options: 2 MB
20 MB
200 MB
2 GB
questions.explanation: 10,000 x 2 KB is 20,000 KB, or approximately 20 MB. Embeddings, indices, versions, and reports add separate storage costs.

questions.question: Locale metadata is missing for 39% of a dataset, but topic and linguistic scores are high. What is the most defensible report state?
options: Pass, because the aggregate content score is high.
Fail every dimension and delete the snapshot.
Insufficient evidence for the representation claim.
Infer protected attributes from the text to fill the chart.
questions.explanation: Unknown metadata must remain visible. The system cannot make a trustworthy representation claim when the required evidence is incomplete.

questions.question: Why should the analysis pipeline publish a versioned report snapshot instead of making dashboard filters rescan raw text?
options: It keeps interactive reads fast and makes the decision reproducible from a complete manifest.
It prevents customers from viewing any underlying examples.
It removes the need to isolate tenants and projects.
It guarantees that topic models never drift.
questions.explanation: Materialized report snapshots provide low-latency aggregates and preserve the exact dataset, feature, taxonomy, metric, and target versions behind a decision.

questions.question: A report finds that 63% of prompts share one instruction template even though they cover many topics. Which remediation best addresses the diagnosed failure?
options: Collect more examples with the same template.
Infer missing demographic attributes.
Cluster template families, remove excess copies, and rewrite prompt forms.
Raise the overall score threshold without changing the data.
questions.explanation: The failure is linguistic repetition, not missing topic volume. Template cleanup directly repairs the cause and limits the stages that need recomputation.

questions.question: Which condition is required before a new diversity report becomes the customer-visible release candidate?
options: At least one analysis job completed successfully.
The overall score increased from the previous run.
All critical jobs completed with aligned dataset, taxonomy, metric, model, and target versions.
The dashboard has no unknown or other category.
questions.explanation: A report is publishable only when its critical evidence is complete and its lineage is internally consistent. Partial or version-mixed results must not replace the prior complete report.
